solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rules covering bureaucratic functionary’s actions

indicators.note: to cover something is to wrap round it, so the first word goes around the second

blocks.note: a suit is slang for a faceless official or office manager

explanation.surface: An office jobsworth's conduct is governed by the regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: LAWS wraps round SUIT, giving LAW-SUIT-S; the ’s stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An action in the legal sense is a case brought before a court, which is what a lawsuit is.

clue.text: Business transaction set up around Pisa oddly became void

indicators.note: oddly points to the first, third and fifth letters of the following word
in a down entry, set up means placed upwards, so the word reads from bottom to top
around tells us the turned word surrounds the other letters

blocks.note: a deal is a business transaction

explanation.surface: A deal involving Pisa fell through.
explanation.definitionFit: A policy or membership that has lapsed has run out and is no longer valid.

clue.text: Red-hot twin would dance for ever

indicators.note: dancing sends the letters whirling into a new order

explanation.surface: A sizzling twin will keep dancing endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the closing phrase of the Christian doxology, 'world without end, Amen'.
explanation.definitionFit: The liturgical phrase means eternally, with no end in time, matching an everlasting duration.

clue.text: American spy books ignored customary practice

indicators.note: the books are ignored, so those letters are left out of the spy word

blocks.note: a spy is a secret agent
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: A US spy disregarded the usual way of doing things with his reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is the habitual or established way something is done, especially in language.

clue.text: Understood by useless Roman orator

blocks.note: tacit means understood without being said
u/s is short for unserviceable, i.e. useless

explanation.surface: Something implied by a hopeless speaker from ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' here means beside, setting the two pieces next to each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacitus, best known as a historian, was also a celebrated advocate and public speaker in Rome.

clue.text: Feeling of loathing when not available to take drugs away at first

indicators.note: at first picks out only the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: NA is the abbreviation for not available
to use is slang for taking drugs

explanation.surface: An addict feels revulsion when there are no drugs to be had.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea is sickness, and by extension intense disgust or revulsion toward something.

clue.text: Striking soldiers heading north remain popular? Good

indicators.note: in a down entry, heading north means travelling upwards, so the letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: to rest is to stay or remain

explanation.surface: Soldiers on strike march off northward and ask whether staying put would be well received.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arresting catches the eye and holds attention, just as something striking does.

clue.text: I curtsey trembling with some degree of alarm perhaps

indicators.note: trembling shakes the letters out of their order

blocks.note: a measure is an amount or degree, as in 'some measure of success'

explanation.surface: Someone bobs a nervous curtsey, showing a certain amount of fright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alarm' looks like fear, matching the trembling, but here it is a burglar alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A burglar alarm is one example of a protective device installed to keep property safe.

clue.text: Shortened game after a delay at the start

indicators.note: after puts the game behind the single letter a in the sequence
at the start keeps only the opening letter of the word before

explanation.surface: A match was cut short after a hold-up at the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: An abridged text has been cut down in length, condensed from the full version.

clue.text: Standard fastener gripping Nationalist leader in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter
gripping means holding on to, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: par is the standard or norm

explanation.surface: A political party leader is being restrained by an ordinary clasp.
explanation.definitionFit: Parlance is a particular way of using words, a vocabulary or idiom of a group.

clue.text: My return interrupting German shopkeeper

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the exclamation is read backwards
interrupting means breaking into the middle of something

blocks.note: cor and my are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone's return home cuts in on a German shopkeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is the exclamation, like British 'cor!', not the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A grocer is a trader who runs a shop selling food and household provisions.

clue.text: Had on with open hostility in speech

indicators.note: in speech means we use how the word sounds when spoken, not its spelling

blocks.note: war is open hostility; in a non-rhotic British accent the two words sound alike

explanation.surface: Someone dressed in a certain way while voicing outright aggression.
explanation.definitionFit: If you wore something you had it on your body, the past tense of wearing clothes.

clue.text: Supply with oddly missing beans directly

indicators.note: with the odd letters missing, only the even-numbered letters are kept

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters of beans
due means directly, as in due north

explanation.surface: Someone is told to hand over the beans straight away, though some are curiously absent.
explanation.definitionFit: To endue is to endow or provide someone with a quality or gift.

clue.text: Pocketed note about rabble follower close to dad

indicators.note: about means around, so the note wraps the next piece
the close of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
the word following rabble in rabble-rouser

explanation.surface: A dad's message concerns someone who trails after the mob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rabble follower' suggests a hanger-on, but it means the word that comes after 'rabble'.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouser money is informal British for putting it in your pocket, often dubiously.

clue.text: Examples of types of mushroom mostly found in baked dishes

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
found in places the shortened word inside the dishes

blocks.note: a cep is a kind of edible mushroom

explanation.surface: Varieties of mushroom tend to turn up in baked food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'types of mushroom' reads as a phrase, but 'Examples of types' is the definition and only 'mushroom' is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Pieces are individual items or specimens of a kind, such as pieces of furniture or art.

clue.text: Intense passion on X? Better not get caught up in it

definitions.text: Better not get caught up in it

blocks.note: fire is strong passion or ardour

explanation.surface: Fierce feeling about a cross on a ballot paper, and a warning to stay clear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' means next to: the passion follows the X.
explanation.definitionFit: Being caught in crossfire means being hit by shots from two directions, something anyone would want to avoid.

clue.text: Letter of introduction initially spelt wrongly without ‘e’ at the end

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word it follows
spelt wrongly means the letters come out in the wrong order
at the end places the quoted letter after everything else

explanation.surface: A letter of introduction has been misspelt, missing its final e.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside, so the E is added at the end rather than removed.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a formal letter, like those of the apostles in the New Testament.

clue.text: Actively press to include key hymnbooks

indicators.note: actively suggests the letters are on the move and get rearranged
to include means to take something inside

blocks.note: Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: An instruction to push hard on a key.
explanation.definitionFit: Psalters are books containing the psalms, used for singing in worship.

clue.text: Head of Siemens becomes less enthusiastic about earliest of hybrid trains

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
the earliest letter of a word is its first
about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: someone who cools on an idea becomes less keen

explanation.surface: The Siemens chief goes off the idea of the first hybrid locomotives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trains' looks like railway stock, apt for Siemens, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to teach or drill them, which is what training them means.

clue.text: Cliff’s lasting effect of grief

blocks.note: first meaning: a steep rocky outcrop on a hillside
second meaning: a mark left on the mind by suffering

explanation.walkthrough: Cliff looks like a man's name with a possessive, but it is a rock face and the ’s means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a rocky precipice and a lingering emotional wound left by trauma.

clue.text: Government of independent ruler in retrospect admitting endless conceit

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is cut off
in retrospect means looking back, so the word is read backwards
admitting means letting in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: an emir is the sovereign ruler of an emirate

explanation.surface: A government led by an autonomous ruler, looked back on, let vanity in.
explanation.definitionFit: A regime is a system or period of rule, especially an authoritarian administration.

clue.text: Fetch each student held captive by rebel

indicators.note: something held captive is shut inside, so these letters sit within the next word

blocks.note: L is a learner, from L-plates
to rise up is to rebel

explanation.surface: Every student taken hostage by an insurgent must be brought back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fetch' is meant in the sense of a price: an item that fetches a sum realises it at sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods sold at auction realise or fetch a certain amount of money for the seller.

clue.text: Niche site originally looking into development of Cree society

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the word
a development changes shape, so the letters are reworked
looking into means peering inside, so the letter goes within the rest

explanation.surface: A site under investigation in the growth of the Cree nation, a Native American people.
explanation.definitionFit: A recess is an alcove or indentation set back into a wall, just as a niche is.

clue.text: State of Scotsman described by girl

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so the girl's name encircles the man's

blocks.note: Ian is the typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A young woman describes the condition a Scottish man is in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like condition, but it is a US state; 'described' means drawn around, not portrayed.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisiana is one of the fifty United States, on the Gulf of Mexico.

clue.text: Appropriate to pursue son’s concern

indicators.note: to pursue is to follow behind, so this word comes after the other

blocks.note: to appropriate is to take for oneself

explanation.surface: A son's business is to seize things.
explanation.definitionFit: A stake is a share or financial interest in a business, which is a concern you hold.

clue.text: Examine closely to maintain weight in fast

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold, so the first word keeps the other inside it

blocks.note: to sift evidence is to examine it closely

explanation.surface: Instructions to scrutinise how weight is kept up during a fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like a period without food, but it is the adjective meaning quick.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift means moving with great speed, a direct synonym of quick or rapid.

clue.text: Protective cover essential to crocodile? Yes in retreat

indicators.note: essential to means at the core of, so the letters lie inside the words
something in retreat goes backwards, so the letters are read right to left

blocks.note: the letters sit across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Is a protective covering vital to a crocodile that is backing away? Yes.
explanation.walkthrough: Crocodiles really do have a third, transparent eyelid, so the surface is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyelid is the fold of skin that closes to shield and protect the eye.

clue.text: Josh to deliver one tricky clue

indicators.note: tricky suggests the letters have been twisted into a different order

blocks.note: to rid or deliver someone of something is to free them
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A man named Josh is to hand over a difficult crossword clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Josh looks like a name, but it is the verb meaning to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: To josh is to tease or make fun of someone, which is what ridicule means as a verb.

clue.text: Unexpected in study on south of France

indicators.note: on means placed next to, joining one piece to the other

blocks.note: a den is a study or private room

explanation.surface: A surprise in a study about the south of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'south of France' looks like the Riviera, but it means the French word for south.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sudden happens quickly and without warning, taking people by surprise.

clue.text: Worried about stress after changing sides

indicators.note: the sides are right and left, so one letter for a side is swapped for the other

blocks.note: taken as written before the swap

explanation.surface: Anxiety about pressure once someone switches allegiance.
explanation.walkthrough: R (right) in the stress word becomes L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: Restless means uneasy and unable to settle, the state of someone who is worried.
